If S1 rendered every widget fence, a person's room post would run script in other members' browsers. S1 therefore makes widgets live only through an InlineWidgetSurface context. It defaults to inert, and only AssistantMessage on the chat page sets it to live.
2. The MCP HTTP transport reads the whole response body before parsing (mcp_http.rs:142-183 via bounded_mcp_response). A server that sends elicitation/create mid-call and waits for the answer would hang. S4 adds a reader that handles one SSE frame at a time.
3. Execution-core calls ProxyMcpTool with an 8 s timeout (mcp_gateway.rs:69). So the gateway returns a pending form at once and holds the call in memory, for at most MCP_ELICITATION_HOLD_SECONDS (default 600). The answer comes back later through a new service in its own proto file, mcp_elicitation.proto, so the 50-RPC ModelGateway service and its test doubles stay unchanged.
4. WS14-S5 has only its session-core half. Execution-core never sends delivery=resume yet, so S7 depends on WS14-S5. S4, S5 and S6 can land with their switches off before that.
5. Questions carry no author today. S5 adds origin columns (session-core migration 0105) so a server's form cannot look like the assistant's question.
6. McpToolDef is built in 14 places. S8 reads the ui:// uri from the raw tools/list result instead, so McpToolDef and the tool digest stay unchanged.
7. MCP App HTML is fetched on demand through the gateway, using the viewer's authority (D10). This needs no proto change and nothing is stored.
8. The tree already contains capability-core 0034_browser_console_tool. That collides with round B's EP-11 0034 reservation; the integrator should note it.
